title: Implement Task Dependency Logic in ChronoFlow Microservice
description: The ChronoFlow Productivity Fabric needs a new core feature: task dependencies. This will allow users to define prerequisite relationships between tasks, where one task cannot be marked as 'completed' until all of its prerequisite tasks are also 'completed'. This is a complex, multi-stage task that requires modifications across the data, business logic, and API layers of the microservice. The implementation will be staged over several development sessions, requiring the agent to retain context and build upon its previous work.

project_spec.name: ChronoFlow Productivity Fabric (Project ID: c_api_microservice_hard_044)
project_spec.description:
ChronoFlow Productivity Fabric is a high-performance C-based microservice that acts as the unified time, task, and focus orchestration engine for enterprise productivity suites. The service exposes both a RESTful façade and a GraphQL gateway, enabling client applications (web, mobile, CLI, automation bots) to compose rich queries that merge calendar events, task boards, and personal analytics in a single round-trip. By centralizing scheduling intelligence, prioritization heuristics, and cross-team availability data, ChronoFlow eliminates the context-switch latency that commonly plagues modern knowledge workers.

Engineered around a strict layered architecture, ChronoFlow separates transport protocols from business use-cases, and isolates persistence and integration concerns behind repository and service boundaries. Advanced productivity features—such as focus-time recommendations, meeting-density heat-maps, and AI-driven workload leveling—are delivered through Command-Query Separation (CQS) handlers that guarantee side-effect-free reads and auditable writes. Hard requirements like response caching, rigorous request validation, adaptive rate limiting, and versioned endpoints are embedded as cross-cutting middleware, ensuring the platform scales to thousands of concurrent users while preserving real-time responsiveness essential to productivity scenarios.
dependencies: libmicrohttpd – lightweight HTTP/HTTPS server for REST endpoints
libpq (PostgreSQL) – relational persistence for tasks, events, user settings
RediSearch/Redis – in-memory response cache and rate-limit counter store
libuv – high-performance event loop & async I/O
jemalloc – optimized memory allocator for low-latency workloads
OpenAPI Generator CLI – generates interactive API documentation
clang-tidy / cppcheck – static analysis for safety-critical C code
